transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
President Trump got a lot of attention
in last night's Senate debate in Maine less than a month before
the November midterm elections.
Republican incumbent Susan Collins is facing Democratic
challenger Troy Jackson as she seeks a sixth term in the Senate.
During the debate in Portland, Collins,
a moderate, described herself as not being the president's
favorite senator as she criticized the war with Iran.
>> It is not well thought out.
It has caused adverse circumstances in terms
of the cost of global oil.
>> Prices of oil, gasoline, and diesel
have jumped sharply since the US and Israel began attacking Iran
more than seven months ago.
Jackson is a former state senator.
He says his focus is on what people in Maine want.
>> Senator Collins has had 30 years
to show whose side she's on.
I don't owe Donald Trump and the billionaires anything.
I don't fight for billionaires like she does.
I owe Maineers everything, and that's
who I'm going to be fighting for when I'm the next US senator.
>> Jackson was the state Senate's president and majority
leader from 2018 to 2024.
When President Trump announced his MAGA Inc. super PAC
would start paying for ads promoting his administration,
it was not clear what that would mean for the ads that
had already aired.
NPR's Tamara Keith reports that's now coming into focus.
>> The White House insisted the ads were public service
announcements meant to promote patriotism.
But lawmakers from both sides of the aisle
criticized taxpayer dollars going
to what looked like political advertisements.
On Monday, Trump announced MAGA Inc.
would take over funding the ads.
But a White House official not authorized
to speak on the record confirmed that didn't mean
this super PAC would reimburse taxpayers for the ads that
have already aired.
According to Ad Impact, the US government
has spent more than $11.5 million
to air the ads nationwide.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
>> Oscar-winning actress Eva Marie Saint
has died at the age of 102.
NPR's Colin Dwyer says the big screen star
had leading roles in film classics,
such as On the Waterfront and North by Northwest.
>> Back in 2014, 60 years after the release of On the Waterfront,
Eva Marie Saint told NPR she had no idea
that they were making a classic.
>> Of course not.
You just want to do the best you can.
You take each day at a time.
I don't think anyone ever knows.
>> At the age of 30, it was her first feature film,
and she won an Oscar for it.
She went on to play the femme fatale in Alfred Hitchcock's
North by Northwest.
And later in her career, in 1990,
she won an Emmy for her TV work.
Colin Dwyer, NPR News.
>> Wall Street futures are mostly lower this morning.
Dow futures are off 19 points.
This is NPR News from Washington.
A new report looks at the effectiveness
of parental controls and safety features introduced by Open AI
when it rolled out Chat GPT for teenagers earlier this year.
NPR's Ritu Chatterjee says the report
finds the Chatbot still poses risks to adolescents.
>> Researchers at the online safety advocacy group
Common Sense Media tested Chat GPT
before and after the launch of Chat GPT for teens.
They found that some of the advertised safety measures,
like the Chatbot's refusal to engage
in explicit sexual role play with teens, do work,
but other measures don't.
For example, in most cases,
parents did not receive alerts
when teen accounts created by the researchers
explicitly discussed self-harm, suicide, or disordered eating.
And Chat GPT still interacts with teens like a friend.
Tom Siegel is executive director
of Common Sense Media's Youth AI Safety Institute
and was involved in the research.
>> There are, you know, some improvement in some areas,
but we feel it still creates a huge risk for kids
that it is too personable in those interactions.
>> Ritu Chatterjee, NPR News.
The French government says nearly 500 people were detained
during yesterday's nationwide protests over school funding
and the condition of schools in the country.
The Interior Ministry says more than a quarter million people
took part in the demonstration nationwide.
In Paris, small groups of protesters clashed
with riot police who used tear gas against some of them.
Those protests began a couple of weeks ago.
I'm Dave Mattingly, NPR News, in Washington.
>> Want to hear this podcast without sponsor breaks?
Amazon Prime members can listen to NPR News Now
sponsor free through Amazon Music.
Or you can also support NPR's vital journalism
and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.

topics.text: Maine Senate debate: Incumbent Republican Susan Collins and Democratic challenger Troy Jackson debate one month before midterm elections
Trump's MAGA Inc. super PAC to fund political ads; government spent $11.5 million on ads already aired without reimbursement
Oscar-winning actress Eva Marie Saint dies at age 102; starred in On the Waterfront and North by Northwest
Wall Street futures mostly lower; Dow futures off 19 points
Report finds OpenAI's ChatGPT safety features for teens partially ineffective; parental alerts for self-harm discussions mostly fail
French government detains nearly 500 people during nationwide protests over school funding and conditions; over 250,000 participated
